data.title: The chairs left after closing

memoryNodes.cue: Each person speaks about the arrangement.
They consider people affected by changes.
memoryNodes.cueZh: 大家考虑调整影响到的人。
他们带着约定一起离开。

data.situation:
On Thursday, the three chairs stayed beside the staff table after closing. Mina placed the unfinished rota in the middle. The hierarchy was simple: she managed the shop, and Jay and Noor reported to her. Their roles were subordinate to hers in that arrangement, but they knew things she did not. Jay said that repeated unpaid extra work would exploit the staff rather than solve the machine problem. Noor agreed that avoiding exploitation mattered as much as keeping the door open. They listed the other stakeholders: waiting customers, the supplier and the owner of the building. A plan had to be aligned with the time and money they actually had. Mina moved one scheduled collection to the following week and wrote down who would make the call. When the table was clear, they went out through the front door together. THURSDAY — AGREED CHANGES
Move one scheduled collection to next week; Jay will call the customer.
Use paid, scheduled time for the repair backlog.
Noor will confirm Saturday counter hours.
Mina will speak to the repairer and supplier before the next rota is finalised.

readingBlocks.en: On Thursday, the three chairs stayed beside the staff table after closing. Mina placed the unfinished rota in the middle. The hierarchy was simple: she managed the shop, and Jay and Noor reported to her. Their roles were subordinate to hers in that arrangement, but they knew things she did not. Jay said that repeated unpaid extra work would exploit the staff rather than solve the machine problem. Noor agreed that avoiding exploitation mattered as much as keeping the door open. They listed the other stakeholders: waiting customers, the supplier and the owner of the building. A plan had to be aligned with the time and money they actually had. Mina moved one scheduled collection to the following week and wrote down who would make the call. When the table was clear, they went out through the front door together.
readingBlocks.zh: 周四关门后，三把椅子仍留在员工桌旁。米娜把没完成的排班表放在中间。等级关系很简单：她管理店铺，杰伊和努尔向她汇报。在这个安排里，他们的职位低于她，但也知道她不知道的事情。杰伊说，反复无偿加班会压榨员工，并不能解决机器问题。努尔同意，避免剥削与维持营业同样重要。他们列出其他利益相关者：等待的顾客、供应商和房屋所有人。计划必须与实际的时间和钱相符。米娜把一项原定取件改到下周，写下谁打电话。桌面清空后，三人一起从前门离开。

readingBlocks.en:
THURSDAY — AGREED CHANGES
Move one scheduled collection to next week; Jay will call the customer.
Use paid, scheduled time for the repair backlog.
Noor will confirm Saturday counter hours.
Mina will speak to the repairer and supplier before the next rota is finalised.
readingBlocks.zh:
周四——商定的调整
一项原定取件改到下周，杰伊联系顾客。
在安排好的付薪工作时间内处理积压维修。
努尔确认周六柜台时间。
下一版排班确定前，米娜联系维修师傅和供应商。

glossary.zh: 按权力或级别组织的等级体系
glossary.note: a hierarchy；本课管理级别，不计统治集团作为另一单位。
glossary.example: The shop had a simple hierarchy.
glossary.exampleZh: 小店有简单的等级体系。

externalEvidence.definition: the organization of people at different ranks in an administrative body

glossary.zh: 在级别或职位上较低的
glossary.note: subordinate to + 上级；本句形容词，不是作为动词使次要或名词下属。
glossary.example: Jay’s role was subordinate to Mina’s in the shop hierarchy.
glossary.exampleZh: 在小店等级安排中，杰伊的职位低于米娜。

glossary.zh: 为自身利益不公平地使用或压榨别人
glossary.note: exploit someone：为自身利益不公平地利用或压榨别人。
glossary.example: Repeated unpaid extra work would exploit the staff.
glossary.exampleZh: 反复无偿额外工作会压榨员工。

externalEvidence.definition: use or manipulate to one's advantage

glossary.zh: 为了自身利益不公平地利用或剥削别人
glossary.note: the exploitation of workers：剥削工人；本句不是中性开发资源。
glossary.example: They wanted to avoid the exploitation of staff.
glossary.exampleZh: 他们希望避免剥削员工。

externalEvidence.definition: an act that exploits or victimizes someone (treats them unfairly)

glossary.zh: 会受到某项活动或决定影响的利益相关者
glossary.note: stakeholder：受决定影响或对结果有利益关系的人；shareholder：股东。
glossary.example: The waiting customers were stakeholders in the shop’s plan.
glossary.exampleZh: 等待的顾客是小店计划的利益相关者。
